A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same δ-Conservative Search work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, added and removed material to be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original biological sequence-design experiments, proxy-failure analyses and ablations in Section 6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds RL-objective comparisons, protein-data robustness tests and GFP benchmark results. Appendix B.5 explicitly distinguishes borrowed comparator results.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix B.2 adds δ-CS variants using SQL, VarGrad and Soft PCL training objectives beyond the original trajectory-balance implementation. The central rank-based sampling, Bernoulli masking, sequential denoising and uncertainty-adaptive δ rule remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix B.5 adds GFP Medium and Hard benchmark scenarios characterized by low-scoring initial sequences distant from high-fitness sequences. This extends coverage within protein design; the existing biological task families, including AMP and Hard TF-Bind-8, were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds TuRBO to all six main benchmark comparisons, LS-GFN back-and-forth search in Sections 6.4 and B.3–B.4, and SQL, VarGrad and Soft PCL comparisons in B.2. LatProtRL also enters the additional GFP comparison through explicitly literature-sourced results in Table 4.

E3.justification: Added protocols include 1,000-example GFP/AAV initialization tests, AAV reward-percentile truncations, LS-GFN backtracking matched through K=δL, and expanded δ sweeps. The additional GFP benchmark uses 15 rounds with 256 queries per round; the retained FLEXS experiments still use 10 rounds with 128 queries.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled search-strategy comparisons, alternative RL-objective analyses, reduced-data and degraded-proxy tests, and broader δ sensitivity and Pareto analyses. Conversely, v1 Appendix B.4's rank-reweighted proxy-training ablation is removed. Existing Hard TF-Bind-8 and RNA adaptive-δ studies are retained and reorganized.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent runs and retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting for matched results. No changed run count, seed-reporting scheme, confidence-interval procedure or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Original Appendix C and AMP table values are retained, but v2 adds substantial results for new comparators, RL objectives, robustness tests and parameter sweeps. Table 4 newly reports GFP Medium/Hard scores of 1.06 ± 0.1 and 0.86 ± 0.0 at δ=0.01 under the added benchmark protocol. The rank-reweighting ablation results are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical core, including the trajectory-balance objective and masking/denoising distributions, is retained. Expanded discussion of GFlowNet/RL equivalences cites existing work and introduces no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains uncertainty-adaptive conservative off-policy search that improves biological sequence design while balancing exploration and proxy reliability. The introduction and conclusion retain the same DNA, RNA, protein and peptide claims; added experiments primarily support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains arbitrary-position masking versus LS-GFN's suffix edits, connects smaller δ to uncertainty on harder GFP scenarios, and explicitly acknowledges that δ-CS does not resolve underlying active-learning and proxy-estimation weaknesses. These elaborate and qualify v1's retained conservative-search interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents δ clipping, TuRBO's continuous-to-one-hot conversion and the LS-GFN matching rule. Conversely, v1's stated 1,000 policy updates and exact 1,000-sequence AMP query budget are no longer specified. Core architectures, most hyperparameters and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands related work with a dedicated GFlowNets subsection covering foundations, credit assignment, exploration and RL connections, plus additional trust-region and generative Bayesian optimization research. It explicitly distinguishes δ-CS from exploration methods that assume accurate rewards and develops its relationship to LS-GFN.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are edited, experiments are reorganized to lead with proxy failure, FLEXS tasks are grouped, and AMP and pseudocode move into the appendices. Related work gains thematic subsections, and the conclusion gains limitations and discussion. This substantially reorganizes the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The main text adopts two columns, with new radar, robustness and sensitivity displays. Pseudocode is split and relocated, the proxy-correlation bar chart becomes a numerical table, and main benchmark curves display means instead of medians. The maximum-summary and rank-ablation tables are removed; the AMP table is relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens direct testing of the central robustness claim through matched LS-GFN comparisons, degraded-proxy experiments, broader δ sensitivity tests and harder GFP evaluation. These address v1's limited validation of robustness and generality. Removing the rank-reweighting ablation, omitting budget details and introducing Figure 9's conflicting mean/median labels weaken documentation, but the more informative validation and explicit limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
